question.problem:
The table below gives the values of a continuous function $f(x)$ on the closed interval $[0,15]$ with a regular step size. If the right Riemann sum approximation to the area under the curve $y=f(x)$ with $3$ subintervals defined by the given points has a value of $60$, then what must be the value of $k?$

| $x$ | $0$ | $5$ | $10$ | $15$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $f(x)$ | $2$ | $3$ | $4$ | $k$ |
question.worked_solution:
The area $A$ under the graph can be approximated using the formula

$$
A≈(\overset{\text{heights}}{\overset{⏞}{f(5)+f(10)+f(15)}})\cdot {{Δx}_{⏟}}_{\text{width}}.
$$

So, we now set up a table with the values of $f(x)$ at each point:

| $x$ | $5$ | $10$ | $15$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $f(x)$ | $3$ | $4$ | $k$ |

Now, we obtain the following approximation for the area:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & ≈(3+4+k)\cdot 5 \\  & =(7+k)\cdot 5 \\  & =5k+35\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, since we are given that $A$ must be  $60,$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}5k+35 & =60 \\ 5k & =60-35 \\ k & =\frac{25}{5} \\ k & =5.\end{aligned}
$$
